common_name: Shooting Star Mountain Laurel (Reflexed Star-Shaped Flower Selection)

planting.note: Set container-grown plants in spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil and mulch to keep roots cool. Shooting Star is prized for its deeply cut, fully reflexed white petals that curl back into a distinctive pinwheel or star shape rather than the typical cupped mountain laurel bloom.

directions: Plant in dappled woodland light or morning sun with afternoon shade, especially in warmer zones, and avoid alkaline or poorly drained sites. This vigorous, upright selection blooms heavily in early summer, with each flower opening into a starry, pinwheel-like form that sets it apart from standard bell-shaped mountain laurel cultivars. Established plants need only supplemental water during drought and benefit from an acidic mulch such as pine bark or needles.

planting.note: Install in spring in acidic, well-drained soil enriched with organic matter, siting where roots stay cool and moist but never waterlogged. Firecracker is grown as much for its deep burgundy-red spring growth flush as for its rich red buds opening to pink summer flowers.

directions: Give this vigorous, upright cultivar part shade in the South and it will tolerate more sun farther north as long as soil moisture is consistent. New leaves emerge a striking wine-red before maturing to glossy dark green, adding color well before the flower buds open in early summer. Prune only lightly right after bloom to preserve next year's flower buds, and keep a deep organic mulch layer to protect the shallow root system.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Transplant in spring into acidic, humus-rich soil with reliable drainage; raised beds or slopes help in heavier clay. Carousel is a compact selection whose white flowers carry a bold internal cinnamon-purple band that forms a distinct pinwheel pattern when viewed head-on.

directions: This medium-sized, denser-than-species selection suits foundation plantings and woodland borders where its patterned blooms can be appreciated up close. Provide filtered light and consistently moist, acidic soil, and avoid disturbing the shallow, fibrous root zone once established. Deadheading spent flower clusters redirects energy from seed production back into vegetative growth and next season's bud set.

common_name: Tinkerbell Mountain Laurel (Dwarf Compact Pink Selection)

planting.note: Plant in spring in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil; because of its small mature size it works well in raised beds, rock gardens, or foundation borders. Tinkerbell is a true dwarf mountain laurel with wine-red buds opening to soft pale pink flowers on a dense, slow-growing mound.

directions: Because of its compact, mounding habit this cultivar rarely needs pruning to control size, making it a low-maintenance choice for small gardens where full-size mountain laurels would overwhelm the space. Site it in part shade with acidic, evenly moist soil, and mulch generously to buffer root temperature and moisture swings. Its miniature scale pairs well with dwarf conifers and other acid-loving companion shrubs in mixed woodland borders.

planting.note: Set out container stock in spring in acidic, well-drained, organically rich soil and keep the root zone consistently cool and moist. Keepsake is one of the most sought-after banded cultivars, with dark maroon buds opening to silvery-white flowers marked by a bold burgundy interior band.

directions: Grow in part shade with protection from harsh afternoon sun and drying winds, particularly in warmer parts of its range, to keep foliage from bronzing or scorching. The dramatic banded flower pattern shows best when plants receive even moisture through the bud-set and bloom period in late spring to early summer. Avoid heavy fertilization, which can push soft growth prone to leaf spot; a yearly topdressing of acidic compost is usually sufficient.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil, choosing a site with morning sun and afternoon shade for best flower color retention. Bandeau produces white flowers wrapped in an unusually wide, dark maroon interior stripe that resembles a headband circling each bloom.

directions: This heavy-blooming selection benefits from a thick acidic mulch layer to conserve soil moisture and moderate temperature around its shallow roots. Its wide, contrasting flower band is most vivid on plants grown in bright, filtered light rather than deep shade, where flowering is reduced. Light shaping right after the bloom period keeps the naturally rounded form dense without sacrificing next year's flower buds.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into acidic, well-drained soil amended with leaf mold or pine bark fines to mimic native woodland duff. Freckles bears white flowers speckled throughout with fine maroon-red spotting, giving each bloom a freckled, hand-painted look distinct from plain white cultivars.

directions: Grow this medium-to-large selection in a partly shaded woodland setting where its speckled flowers can be viewed against dark evergreen foliage. Consistent soil moisture during bud formation in late spring improves both flower count and the visibility of the maroon spotting. Established plants are drought-tolerant once rooted in but still perform best with supplemental water during extended dry spells in summer.
